Under 42 CFR 456.705, the Medicaid State plan must provide for point-of-sale or point-of-distribution review of drug therapy, using predetermined standards, before each prescription is filled or delivered to the beneficiary or caregiver. That screening must look for seven specified types of potential drug therapy problems, and prospective review also must cover beneficiary counseling standards. findings.statement: The State plan must provide point-of-sale or point-of-distribution review of drug therapy using predetermined standards before each prescription is filled or delivered to the beneficiary or the beneficiary's caregiver [42-CFR-456.705(b)], with an exception for drugs dispensed to residents of nursing facilities that comply with the drug regimen review procedures in 42 CFR part 483 [42-CFR-456.703(b)].

The screening must identify these potential drug therapy problems: (1) therapeutic duplication — two or more drugs from the same therapeutic class where the combined daily dose risks an adverse result or adds program cost without added benefit; (2) drug-disease contraindication; (3) adverse drug-drug interaction; (4) incorrect drug dosage (dosage outside the daily dosage in predetermined standards, calculated as strength x quantity dispensed / day's supply); (5) incorrect duration of drug treatment; (6) drug-allergy interactions; and (7) clinical abuse/misuse [42-CFR-456.705(b), 42-CFR-456.705(b)-2].

Separately from point-of-sale screening, the State plan must provide for a review of drug therapy before each prescription is filled or delivered, and applicable State law (including State Board policy incorporated by reference) must establish standards for counseling the beneficiary or caregiver. The State must give pharmacies detailed compliance information on counseling, profiling, and documentation, which pharmacies must pass on to their pharmacists [42-CFR-456.705(a)].

The same problem categories used for prospective screening (therapeutic duplication, drug-disease contraindication, drug-drug interaction, incorrect dosage, incorrect duration, clinical abuse or misuse) are also monitored retrospectively under 42 CFR 456.709(b), so the prospective screen and the retrospective review use a shared standard set.
